title: Proof Before Permission: Dog Trade Safety Claims Need Public Records
excerpt: Claims about farms, stolen pets, and poison bait need records—not slogans. Vietnam needs transparent quarantine enforcement and a clear path to abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A dog bite can become a death sentence when urgent care fails. Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. Once symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Wash any possible exposure with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, then seek urgent medical assessment for vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies.

Myths cannot replace records

Claims about cyanide bait, stolen companion animals, court convictions, or secret shipments require identifiable police records, court judgments, inspection reports, or named official warnings. No such incident record appears here. Publishing an unverified raid story would fail families, pet owners, and Vietnamese communities demanding honest protection.

Farm claims need traceable proof

“Farm-raised” cannot function as a safety certificate. A responsible supply chain requires traceable origin, lawful transport, veterinary inspection, quarantine compliance, and documented disease controls. Each claim needs records that regulators and communities can inspect. Without them, consumers cannot distinguish lawful activity from theft, illegal transport, or regulatory breach.

Household risk and trade risk both demand control

Household rabies exposure and commercial animal transport are separate biosecurity questions. Neither should be used to imply an unproven causal link. Both require competent veterinary oversight, rapid public-health response, and enforcement against illegal operators. Properly cooked meat is not an established rabies transmission route; handling sick animals, uninspected slaughter, and bites create other serious risks.

Vietnamese communities can set the standard

Families protecting children, pets, and neighborhoods deserve transparent enforcement—not unsupported assurances. SDE calls for complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to a public demand for action. Follow campaign updates on how that demand reaches decision-makers.

Medical guidance: World Health Organization rabies fact sheet.
